title: Unorthodox & Invariable Verbs
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 32; Ryding Ch. 36)
objectives: Use the invariable verbs of praise and blame (نِعْمَ and بِئْسَ).
Conjugate and parse the negative copular verb لَيْسَ (governed like كَانَ).
Use verbs of appropinquation and hope (كَادَ, عَسَى) with imperfect complements.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 13: What case does كَانَ assign to its subject (ism) and predicate (khabar)?

sections.heading: Invariable & Special Verbs
sections.body: Classical Arabic has several special verbs that do not form full tense paradigms. Verbs of praise and blame—نِعْمَ ('how excellent is...') and بِئْسَ ('how evil is...')—remain frozen in the 3ms/3fs past. لَيْسَ ('is not') conjugates only in the past form with present negative meaning. Verbs of nearness and hope—كَادَ ('almost') and عَسَى ('perhaps/may')—take imperfect complements.

sections.label: Governance of لَيْسَ, نِعْمَ, and عَسَى
sections.summary: لَيْسَ governs like كَانَ (nominative ism, accusative khabar). نِعْمَ/بِئْسَ take a definite nominative subject followed by the praised/blamed noun in the nominative. عَسَى typically takes أَنْ + subjunctive imperfect.

sections.heading: Special Verb Constructions
rows: Lying is not beneficial (نَافِعًا = khabar laysa, manṣūb)
How excellent is the truthful servant!
The student almost forgot (imperfect without أَنْ)
May God have mercy on us (أَنْ + subjunctive)

sections.translation: Righteousness is not by speech alone.
sections.irab: لَيْسَ: فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ نَاقِصٌ | البِرُّ: اسْمُ لَيْسَ مَرْفُوعٌ | بِالكَلَامِ: خَبَرُ لَيْسَ فِي مَحَلِّ نَصْبٍ
sections.notes: In Classical Arabic, the predicate of لَيْسَ frequently takes the emphatic preposition بِـ (e.g., لَيْسَ بِعَالِمٍ 'he is not a scholar').

sections.heading: لَيْسَ Conjugation
sections.body: لَيْسَ drops its yāʾ before consonant suffixes: لَسْتُ ('I am not'), لَسْتَ ('you are not'), لَسْنَا ('we are not').
